precepts.text: Fourscore men came with their beards shaven, their clothes rent, and having cut themselves; an example of the cutting practice the law forbids.
precepts.point: Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning; the Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“Ye are the children of the Lord your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.” Jeremiah shows the very practice the law forbids: “there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the Lord.”

Fourscore men, beards shaven, clothes rent, and cut themselves, coming to the house of the Lord that way. Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning, and these customs came from the other nations. It is like the young folks today cutting designs into their eyebrows; we are not supposed to be doing that.

The Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

precepts.text: Asa fortified Mizpah in his war with Baasha king of Israel, and that pit became the grave Ishmael used.
precepts.point: The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

precepts.why:
The pit Ishmael filled with the eighty men he slew “was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel”. Kings shows when: “Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none was exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.”

Asa fortified Mizpah in his war with Baasha king of Israel, with the stones and timber of Ramah. The pit dug for fear of Baasha during that war became the grave Ishmael used, when he went out from Mizpah weeping, playing a part, invited the men in to Gedaliah, and slew them in the midst of the city, sparing only the ten that had treasures of wheat, barley, oil and honey hidden in the field.

points: In the seventh month Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed and a prince of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at a banquet held in Ishmael's honor.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael and his ten men rose up and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam with the sword and slew him, the governor the king of Babylon had made over the land.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael also slew all the Jews with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldeans and men of war that were found there.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: The second day after the murder, before anyone knew of it, eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria with their beards shaven, their clothes rent, and their bodies cut, bringing offerings and incense to the house of the Most High.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael went out from Mizpah weeping as he met them, playing a part, and invited them in to Gedaliah; when they came into the midst of the city he and his men slew them and cast them into a pit.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ten of the eighty were spared when they told Ishmael they had hidden treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people at Mizpah, including the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan had committed to Gedaliah, and departed toward the Ammonites.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: When Johanan and the captains heard of all the evil Ishmael had done, not only killing Gedaliah but at least eighty other men, they took their men and went to fight him and found him by the great waters in Gibeon.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: All the people Ishmael had taken captive were glad to see Johanan, turned about, and returned to him, but Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Johanan took the whole remnant he had recovered from Ishmael, the mighty men of war, the women, the children, and the eunuchs, and departed to dwell near Bethlehem on the way toward Egypt.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: They set out to seek refuge in Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans, since Ishmael had slain Gedaliah whom the king of Babylon had made governor; with Gedaliah dead they felt they had no reason to stay.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant
